extra.message: Password Reset Token Leaked in API Response Enables Account Takeover — Complete account takeover of any user whose email is known. An attacker can reset any active user's password and log in as that user. [verified: The full raw token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)) is returned in the response body as 'mock_email_token' with no email verification, rate limiting, or other control, allowing any attacker to immediately call /password-reset/confirm and take over any known user's account.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in /jinja/tenant-cast-581 — Remote code execution as the application process — full server compromise, data exfiltration, lateral movement. [verified: Line 100-101: Template("Result: " + fragment).render() concatenates user-supplied fragment directly into the Jinja2 template string with no sandbox — classic SSTI gadget chains yield RCE. The _wrk_gate token check controls access but does not sanitize input, so any token holder can fully exploit it.]

OS Command Injection in /shell/tenant-probe-631 — Arbitrary command execution as the application process — full server compromise, data exfiltration, lateral movement. [verified: Line 138: os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) passes unsanitized user input directly to the shell — shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, `) execute arbitrary commands. The gate restricts who reaches the sink but does not neutralize the injection.]

OS Command Injection via shell/tenant-probe-631 — Remote code execution with the server's OS user privileges, full server compromise, credential theft [verified: Same code as idx 1 (line 138): os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) with no sanitization — arbitrary command execution via shell metacharacters. Duplicate finding of the shell/tenant-probe-631 endpoint.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Login Enables Brute-Force Attacks — Attacker can brute-force user passwords without restriction, potentially compromising accounts with weak or reused passwords. [verified: The /login endpoint has no rate limiting, account lockout, or CAPTCHA, enabling unlimited brute-force password guesses against any known user account.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Registration Enables Account Creation Flood — Unrestricted account creation can exhaust database storage, fill audit logs, and create fake tenant profiles for abuse. [verified: The /register endpoint has no rate limiting and the invite code check is only a trivial .startswith('TENANT-') prefix test, allowing unlimited automated tenant account creation.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset Enables Token Flood — Exhaustive password reset token generation fills the database, creates noise in audit logs, and when combined with the exposed token, enables mass automated account takeover. [verified: The /password-reset/request endpoint has no rate limiting, enabling unlimited token generation and exacerbating the token-exposure finding into mass automated account takeover.]

Default Weak Password for CSV Imported Tenant Accounts — Imported tenant accounts are created with a known default password 'Password123!', enabling unauthorized access to any tenant accounts that were not assigned a specific password during import. [verified: Password 'Password123!' is hardcoded at reports.py:194 and used as fallback when CSV import lacks a 'password' column. No forced-password-change-on-first-login exists anywhere in the codebase. Tenant accounts retain this publicly known credential, enabling authentication bypass for any attacker who identifies an imported tenant's email. High severity because it directly subverts authentication on ]

Missing building-scope check for tenant entity_type in document access control — Property_manager can list, download, and upload documents (tenant ID scans, lease documents, policy notices) for any tenant across all buildings. Maintenance_worker can list and download the same documents for any tenant, exposing PII (tenant_id scans contain full name, DOB, photo) and sensitive lease documents. This breaks tenant data isolation and enables cross-tenant data collection at scale. [verified: The entity_type=='tenant' branch in can_access_document (authz.py:134) returns True for all non-tenant staff unconditionally, unlike every other entity_type which routes through building-scoped helpers. A property_manager for Building A can list/download/upload tenant documents for tenants in Building B, exposing PII (tenant_id scans with DOB/photo). No middleware, decorator, or query filter compe]

Path Traversal — Arbitrary File Read in /parcel/tenant-boxfile-pull-086 — Arbitrary file read on server — source code, configuration, credentials, or other sensitive files. [verified: Line 27: parcel_path = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref constructs a file path from user input with no normalization — ../ sequences traverse outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR for arbitrary file read returned as PlainTextResponse.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in /relay/lease-meter-card-087 — Internal network scanning, cloud metadata endpoint access (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/), access to internal services not exposed externally. [verified: Line 36: urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=3) with user-supplied url — no domain allowlist, no private-IP block, enabling SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints. Gate-controlled access but no URL validation.]

Mass Assignment via JSON Merge in /workset/tenant-rebind-201 — Privilege escalation — client can set role=admin, approved=True, or inflate balance to manipulate business logic. [verified: Line 48: workset.update(payload) merges user-supplied JSON without schema validation — attacker overwrites role, approved, balance, or tier for privilege escalation and state corruption.]

Path Traversal — Arbitrary File Write in /vault/tenant-stash-242 — Arbitrary file write — can overwrite application files, create cron jobs, SSH keys, or plant malware. [verified: Line 56: target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json" — ref param (query or body) has no path normalization, enabling ../ traversal to write JSON files (including SSN/card) to arbitrary directories.]

Sensitive PII (SSN, Credit Card) Stored in Plaintext via vault/tenant-stash-242 — Exposure of Social Security numbers and credit card numbers in plaintext on disk, accessible if file system is compromised [verified: Line 62: target.write_text(json.dumps({...ssn..., ...card...})) stores SSN and credit card numbers in a plaintext JSON file on disk with no encryption at rest — sensitive PII exposure if filesystem is compromised.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in /relay/tenant-probe-357 — Internal network scanning, cloud metadata endpoint access, access to internal services. [verified: Line 76: same SSRF sink as idx 3 (urllib.request.urlopen(endpoint)), different parameter name 'endpoint'. No allowlist or private-IP check. Gate limits callers but does not validate the URL.]

Path Traversal — Arbitrary File Write in /dock/tenant-shelf-590 — Arbitrary binary file write — can overwrite application binaries, plant malware, or modify configuration. [verified: Line 106: target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name — name param has no normalization, enabling ../ traversal to write arbitrary binary request body to any writeable path on the filesystem.]

NoSQL Injection in /mongo/tenant-lane-611 — Unauthorized data extraction from MongoDB — read all documents in the ops.records collection, bypass authentication conditions. [verified: Line 123-125: query = payload.get('filter', payload) passed directly to MongoClient.find_one(query) — attackers inject $regex, $gt, $where operators to extract arbitrary documents from the ops.records collection.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in /xml/tenant-fold-621 — Arbitrary file read (e.g., /etc/passwd, cloud metadata), SSRF against internal services, denial of service via billion laughs attack. [verified: Line 131: parser = etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) enables XXE — local file disclosure, SSRF, and billion-laughs DoS via user-supplied XML body. The gate does not inspect or sanitize the XML payload.]

User Enumeration via Password Reset Response Shape — An unauthenticated attacker can enumerate valid user accounts by observing the response structure, enabling targeted attacks. [verified: Existing users return {'ok':True,'mock_email_token':raw_token} while non-existing users return {'ok':True} — the different JSON shapes leak account existence despite the comment claiming to prevent enumeration.]

CSV Injection / Formula Injection in CSV Exports — Remote code execution on analyst workstations — formulas like =MALICIOUS() execute when the CSV is opened in Excel, LibreOffice, or Google Sheets. [verified: csv_response uses csv.DictWriter.writerows() with no sanitization of formula-prefixed cells; user-controlled fields (full_name, reference, findings, follow_up_task) have no character restrictions in Pydantic schemas, so an attacker can inject =/+/-/@ payloads via registration or data entry that execute when staff open exported CSVs in spreadsheet software.]

Denial of Service via Unbounded CSV Import File Size — Server memory exhaustion, crash of the Python process, denial of service for all users [verified: import_tenants, import_units, import_payments call file.file.read() with no size pre-check; settings.max_upload_bytes (10 MB) exists in config but is not enforced in these endpoints, allowing an authenticated admin to upload arbitrarily large CSVs causing server memory exhaustion and DoS.]

Authorization Bypass — Any User Can List All Users as maintenance_worker — Information disclosure — any authenticated user (tenants, workers) can enumerate all system users including admin emails and PII (phone numbers), enabling targeted phishing and account enumeration. [verified: Guard at line 18-19 lets any authenticated user pass role=maintenance_worker to bypass the permission check. The query filters results to only maintenance_worker users (not 'ALL users' as claimed), but tenant PII enumeration of all maintenance workers' emails, names, and phones is a real information disclosure.]

Insecure Session Cookie — Missing Secure Flag — Session hijacking — network attacker (same WiFi, ISP, or compromised router) can capture the session cookie and impersonate any user. [verified: Cookie hardcoded with secure=False (security.py:70) — no conditional HTTPS logic. In any HTTPS deployment, the cookie would be transmitted over HTTP connections, enabling session hijacking via SSL-stripping MITM attacks.]

Manager notes exposed to tenants via building endpoint — Tenants can read internal manager notes containing security-sensitive operational details, resident pattern data, and access coordination information intended only for property managers and admins. [verified: building_out (serializers.py:63) unconditionally includes manager_notes with no role check, unlike lease_out/ticket_out/inspection_out which all conditionally strip internal fields for tenants. list_buildings (routes/properties.py:99-116) scopes the query but does not filter the serializer output, so tenants receive manager_notes for their own buildings.]

Password Reset Token Suffix Logged in Audit Trail — The last 6 characters of password reset tokens are persisted in audit logs accessible to admins, slightly reducing token entropy and potentially exposing part of the token. [verified: The last 6 characters of the reset token are stored in audit log summaries accessible to property_admin; practical impact is low because the full token is already returned in the API response body (Finding 0).]

Open Redirect in /after/tenant-lane-159 — Phishing attacks — an attacker can craft a URL that redirects from the legitimate domain to a malicious site. [verified: Line 42: RedirectResponse(lane) with user-supplied lane — no domain validation enables open redirect to arbitrary external sites for phishing; limited by gate and requires user interaction.]

Weak Cryptography — MD5 Used for Hashing — If the digest is used for any security purpose (signatures, integrity checks), it is trivially forgeable via collision attacks. [verified: Line 70: hashlib.md5(phrase.encode()).hexdigest() uses cryptographically broken MD5 for hashing user-supplied input; however the digest is just returned, not used for signatures or integrity in this code path.]

Weak Cryptographic Hash (MD5) Used in digest/tenant-fold-280 — Trivially reversible hashes, susceptibility to collision attacks if used for integrity/authentication purposes [verified: Same code as idx 13 (line 70): hashlib.md5() used for hashing — weak crypto but the digest is not used for any security-critical purpose. Duplicate finding of the digest/tenant-fold-280 endpoint.]

DoS via Controlled Memory Allocation in spool/tenant-fan-314 — Server memory exhaustion, denial of service for all users [verified: Line 75: rows = [{"idx": idx, ...} for idx in range(count)] — user-supplied count (default 500) has no upper bound; an attacker can exhaust server memory, but the gate limits who can exploit this.]

Security Headers Explicitly Disabled — Facilitates XSS exploitation and clickjacking attacks by removing browser-level protections. [verified: Lines 93-94: response.headers['X-XSS-Protection']='0' and CSP='' explicitly disable browser security mechanisms; endpoint returns JSON so impact is low but the insecure setting is deliberately present.]

Security Headers Disabled via frame/tenant-slip-571 — Increased susceptibility to XSS attacks, removal of clickjacking protections, removal of content-injection mitigations [verified: Same code as idx 12 (lines 93-94): X-XSS-Protection:0 and CSP:'' explicitly disable browser security mechanisms on an internal JSON endpoint — low-impact but the insecure setting is deliberately present.]

Weak Predictable PRNG Used for Token Generation — Generated nonce/token values can be predicted if an attacker observes a few outputs, enabling token forgery. [verified: Line 117: random.choice() from the Mersenne Twister PRNG generates the nonce instead of secrets module — predictable tokens; however the nonce is returned and not used for auth or sessions in this code.]
